extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational linguistics researchers and practitioners working on satire detection, dataset creation, and headline classification (Romanian-language focus)
extracted.subtask_description: Detecting satirical (non-conventional) tone in news headlines, with a focus on Romanian-language, multi-domain headline data and evaluation of machine-learning and deep-learning approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal of a news headline
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary goal of a news headline is to summarize an event in as few words as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the media outlet, a headline can serve as a means to objectively deliver a summary or improve its visibility. This framing constrains what information and stylistic devices a headline can use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines as carriers of satirical tone (stylistic elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific publications may employ stylistic approaches that incorporate the use of sarcasm, irony, and exaggeration, key elements of a satirical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because we consider a headline to be merely a brief summary of the main article, even the headline must reflect the tone of the satirical main content. These stylistic markers (sarcasm, irony, exaggeration) are core signals for labeling or detecting satire in headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current practice: combine headline and main article for detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Current approaches for the Romanian language tend to detect the non-conventional tone (i.e., satire and clickbait) of the news content by combining both the main article and the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates prior-methods' reliance on contextual/full-article information; it serves as a baseline assumption against which headline-only detection should be compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of headline-only satire detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the presence of satirical tone in headlines alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper tests whether headlines by themselves contain sufficient signal for satire detection, evaluating multiple baselines from standard machine learning algorithms to deep learning models to establish feasibility and limits of headline-only approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model comparison and evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare multiple modeling approaches: standard machine-learning algorithms, deep learning models, and Large Language Models (LLMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical comparison is used as the evaluation methodology. The abstract reports that Bidirectional Transformer models outperform both standard machine-learning approaches and LLMs, particularly when the meta-learning Reptile approach is employed — implying metrics should capture such comparative performance and consider meta-learning strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset design: multi-domain Romanian headline dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a multi-domain Romanian news headline dataset (SaRoHead) for the task of detecting satire in headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset should cover multiple domains and be specific to Romanian-language headlines so that models are evaluated on realistic, varied headline distributions; this underpins generalization claims for headline-only satire detection.
